# Price Adjustments

## Why Adjust Prices

- Temporal Normalization: Real estate is a time-sensitive asset.
- Removing "Market Noise"
- Isolation of Physical Value
- Vertical Equity

## Prices After Stabalization
```{python}
# | label: unified_price_adjustment
# | message: false
# | warning: false

df_combined["Adj_Price"] = df_combined["Sold Price"] - df_combined[
    "Concessions Amount"
].fillna(0)
df_combined = df_combined[df_combined["Adj_Price"] > 0].copy()
df_combined["ln_Price"] = np.log(df_combined["Adj_Price"])
df_combined["ln_GLA"] = np.log(df_combined["Total SqFt"].replace(0, np.nan))

start_date = pd.Timestamp("2021-01-01")
lien_date = pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01")
x_days = (df_combined["Sold Date"] - start_date).dt.days.values

pw_model = pwlf.PiecewiseLinFit(x_days, df_combined["ln_Price"].values)
knots_days = pw_model.fit(3)
knot_dates = [start_date + pd.Timedelta(days=int(k)) for k in knots_days]

for i in range(len(knot_dates) - 1):
    col_name = f"Time_{i + 1}"
    start, end = knot_dates[i], knot_dates[i + 1]
    df_combined[col_name] = df_combined["Sold Date"].apply(
        lambda x: max(0, (min(x, end) - start).days / 30.44) if pd.notna(x) else 0
    )

df_combined["Trended_Price"] = df_combined["Adj_Price"].copy()
time_cols = [c for c in df_combined.columns if c.startswith("Time_")]

for seg in ["Residential", "Multi-Family", "Land Sales"]:
    df_seg = df_combined[df_combined["segment"] == seg].copy()
    if len(df_seg) < 20:
        continue
    valid_buckets = [col for col in time_cols if df_seg[col].max() > 0]
    formula = (
        f"ln_Price ~ {' + '.join(valid_buckets)} + ln_GLA + Q('Year Built')"
        if seg != "Land Sales"
        else f"ln_Price ~ {' + '.join(valid_buckets)}"
    )
    try:
        res_ols = smf.ols(
            formula,
            data=df_seg.dropna(
                subset=["ln_GLA", "Year Built"] if seg != "Land Sales" else []
            ),
        ).fit()
        # Trending Logic
        adj_log = 0
        for idx, col in enumerate(time_cols):
            if col in res_ols.params:
                remaining = (
                    (knot_dates[idx + 1] - knot_dates[idx]).days / 30.44
                ) - df_combined.loc[df_combined["segment"] == seg, col]
                adj_log += res_ols.params[col] * np.maximum(0, remaining)
        df_combined.loc[df_combined["segment"] == seg, "Trended_Price"] *= np.exp(
            adj_log
        )
    except:
        pass
```

# Exploratory Analysis

```{python}
# | label: analytics_functions
import umap
import hdbscan
from scipy.stats import rankdata
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA


# --- CORE UTILITIES ---
def get_scaled_data(df):
    # Strictly isolate numbers BEFORE doing any math
    X = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).fillna(0)
    # Remove columns with zero variance (they break PCA)
    X = X.loc[:, X.var() > 1e-4]
    return StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)


def get_umap_embedding(scaled_data, nn, md):
    # Reduce dimensions via PCA first for UMAP stability
    pca_data = PCA(n_components=0.9).fit_transform(scaled_data)
    reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=nn, min_dist=md, random_state=42)
    return reducer.fit_transform(pca_data)


def get_clusters(pca_data, min_size=20):
    clusterer = hdbscan.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=min_size, prediction_data=True)
    return clusterer.fit_predict(pca_data)


# --- VISUALIZATION WRAPPERS ---
def plot_umap_branded(embedding, color_source, title, is_price=True):
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    if is_price:
        price_ranks = rankdata(color_source) / len(color_source)
        scatter = plt.scatter(
            embedding[:, 0],
            embedding[:, 1],
            c=price_ranks,
            cmap="viridis",
            s=10,
            alpha=0.6,
        )
        plt.colorbar(scatter).set_label("Price Percentile (0=Low, 1=High)")
    else:
        unique_labels = np.unique(color_source)
        cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10", len(unique_labels))
        for i, label in enumerate(unique_labels):
            mask = color_source == label
            plt.scatter(
                embedding[mask, 0],
                embedding[mask, 1],
                label=f"Cluster {label}" if label != -1 else "Noise",
                s=15,
                alpha=0.8,
                color=cmap(i),
            )
        plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def plot_pca_heatmap(pca_model, df_features):
    # FIX: Isolate numeric columns specifically to avoid String -> Float errors
    numeric_df = df_features.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).fillna(0)
    kept_columns = numeric_df.columns[numeric_df.var() > 1e-4]

    # Create the loadings dataframe
    loadings_df = pd.DataFrame(pca_model.components_.T, index=kept_columns)

    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
    # Show only top 15 features to keep the heatmap readable
    sns.heatmap(loadings_df.head(15), annot=True, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, fmt=".2f")
    plt.title("PCA Loadings: Feature Correlation to Components")
    plt.show()


# --- EXECUTION ---
# Ensure res_df is defined from the main df_combined
res_df = df_combined[df_combined["segment"] == "Residential"].copy()

# Drop columns that shouldn't be used for clustering/PCA
res_features = res_df.drop(
    columns=["Sold Price", "Adj_Price", "Trended_Price", "List Number", "ParcelId"],
    errors="ignore",
)

res_scaled = get_scaled_data(res_features)
res_pca_model = PCA(n_components=0.9).fit(res_scaled)
res_pca_data = res_pca_model.transform(res_scaled)
res_emb_l = get_umap_embedding(res_scaled, nn=15, md=0.01)
res_l_clusters = get_clusters(res_pca_data, min_size=30)
res_target = res_df["Trended_Price"]
```

## Purposes of Exploratory Analysis

- Validation of Structural Drivers: After trending prices to the 2026 Lien Date, we use Pearson Correlation to confirm that physical characteristics (SqFt, Year Built) are the primary determinants of value, independent of market volatility.
- Identification of Feature Interactions: Real estate value is rarely additive. EDA reveals how variables "handshake". An example of this is how the value of a Finished Basement is conditional on the Total GLA of the home.
- Normalization & Transformation: We identify the need for Log-Scale Transformations. This ensures "Vertical Equity," meaning the model treats a 5% valuation error on a starter home with the same statistical weight as a 5% error on a luxury estate.

# Model Selection & Strategy

## Our Choice: Random Forest

> **Why?** While Gradient Boosting offers slightly higher precision, Random Forest provides superior stability. It is less prone to "overfitting" (hallucinating patterns in the noise), ensuring our valuations are both accurate and statistically defensible.

```{python}
#| label: random_forest
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| cache: true

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, r2_score

# --- DATA PREP ---
res_target_log = np.log1p(res_df["Sold Price"])

# --- MODELING FUNCTIONS ---
def run_log_rf(df_features, target_log, cluster_labels, title):
    # Feature Prep: Combine physical features with UMAP Clusters
    X = df_features.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).copy()
    X["Cluster"] = cluster_labels

    # One-Hot Encode Clusters so the model treats them as categories, not numbers
    X = pd.get_dummies(X, columns=["Cluster"], prefix="C").fillna(0)

    # Split
    X_train, X_test, y_train_log, y_test_log = train_test_split(
        X, target_log, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
    )

    # Train
    rf = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, n_jobs=-1, random_state=42)
    rf.fit(X_train, y_train_log)

    # Predict & Evaluation
    y_pred_log = rf.predict(X_test)
    y_test_dollars = np.expm1(y_test_log)  # Convert log back to actual $
    y_pred_dollars = np.expm1(y_pred_log)

    mae_dollars = mean_absolute_error(y_test_dollars, y_pred_dollars)
    r2 = r2_score(y_test_log, y_pred_log)

    # Performance Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    plt.scatter(y_test_log, y_pred_log, alpha=0.4, color="#2c3e50")
    plt.plot(
        [y_test_log.min(), y_test_log.max()],
        [y_test_log.min(), y_test_log.max()],
        "r--",
        lw=2,
    )
    plt.title(f"{title} Performance\nR² = {r2:.2f} | Avg Error = ${mae_dollars:,.0f}")
    plt.xlabel("Actual Value (Log)")
    plt.ylabel("Predicted Value (Log)")
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.show()

    return rf, X_train, X_test, y_train_log, y_test_log


# random forest
res_model, res_X_train, res_X_test, res_y_train, res_y_test = run_log_rf(
    res_features, res_target_log, res_l_clusters, "Residential Model"
)

```

## Feature Importance

```{python}
# | label: feature_importance_display
# | echo: false

def get_feature_importance_table(model, X_train, title):
    """Returns a table of the top 5 most influential features for the model."""
    importances = model.feature_importances_
    feature_names = X_train.columns

    feat_df = (
        pd.DataFrame({"Feature": feature_names, "Importance (%)": importances * 100})
        .sort_values(by="Importance (%)", ascending=False)
        .head(5)
    )

    feat_df["Dataset"] = title
    return feat_df

res_feat_table = get_feature_importance_table(res_model, res_X_train, "Residential")
res_feat_table[["Feature", "Importance (%)"]]

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
sns.barplot(data=res_feat_table, x="Importance (%)", y="Feature", palette="viridis")
plt.title("Top 5 Value Drivers (Residential Model)")
plt.show()
```
